title: Reading a Contract's Repossession and Collateral Recovery Case History
content:
Compliance memorandum on how the cases of one contract are read together in Repossession and Collateral Recovery.

**1. Cases of the same contract are read together.** Reinstatements are counted across all of the contract's cases against the class maximum of reinstatements after repossession over the life of one contract, and an earlier cured right-to-cure notice on the contract is read across its cases.

- The reinstatement count is the number of the contract's cases whose status is reinstated, over the life of the contract.
- The cured-notice count is the number of right-to-cure notices on earlier cases of the same contract that closed as recalled with the recall reason account brought current, within the rolling 12 months ending on the referral date: the window starts after the same calendar day 12 months earlier, that day itself excluded, and where that month has no such day the last day of that month is used.

**2. A case's money and paper stay with that case.** Expenses, quotes, notices and proceeds of one case belong to that case and its contract only; they are never charged to, offset against or combined with another contract of the same borrower, even when both are in default.

## Points of judgement

| Situation (hypothetical) | Reading |
|---|---|
| A contract had a reinstated case two years ago and now has a recovered case | The earlier reinstated case counts toward the contract's reinstatements. |
| A borrower's second contract shows a surplus after its sale | The surplus is not offset against the expenses of the first contract's case. |
| An earlier case on the same contract closed as recalled after the account was brought current, its cure notice mailed within the 12 months before the new referral | That notice counts as a cured notice on the contract. |
| The same earlier notice was mailed on the same calendar day 12 months before the new referral | It falls outside the window, which excludes that day. |
